Verdict: the reviewer finding is not mathematically valid as stated. The Lévy exponent does not use the full outcome-mark law \(G_a\); it uses only its pushforward by the finite vector \(\Psi_a(y)=(\psi_{a,\tau}(y))_{\tau\in\mathcal T}\). Because the threshold indicators are nested, that finite pushforward law is determined by the coordinate means \(m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}\). Any two \(G_a\)’s having the stated score means induce the same \(H_a\) and hence the same Lévy law.
